themes_detail.label: Residential Waste Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints spiked to 9 this week, up 227% from a 2.8-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, signaling a sudden and acute waste management or illegal dumping problem affecting households across Sheepshead Bay/Gravesend.
evidence: 9 residential disposal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (227% spike, z-score: 5.21)
Spike is most recent and statistically significant among all anomalies
Complaint volume suggests neighborhood-wide impact, not isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Interview residents and sanitation officials to understand whether this reflects a collection failure, new illegal dumping site, or policy change
Check whether spike correlates with any recent sanitation schedule changes or contractor issues in the district

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge in Sheepshead Bay
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 13 last week, up 512% from a 2.1-complaint weekly average, representing a sharp acceleration in visible vandalism across the district.
evidence: 13 graffiti complaints last week vs. 2.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (512% spike, z-score: 5.72)
Highest z-score spike in the dataset, indicating extreme statistical deviation
Recent and sustained over a single week period
reporting_angles: Document graffiti hotspots through field reporting and 311 complaint mapping to identify whether vandalism is concentrated or dispersed
Contact NYPD and Parks enforcement to learn whether there has been any gang activity or organized tagging campaign identified in the district

themes_detail.label: Construction and Plumbing Overload
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints surged to 63 last week, up 234% from an 18.9-complaint weekly average, suggesting either a major infrastructure project or widespread illegal work in the district.
evidence: 63 construction/plumbing complaints last week vs. 18.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (234% spike, z-score: 4.32)
529 total DOB building permits filed in last 90 days across district, with 313 alterations and 83 new buildings, indicating high construction activity
Building/Use complaints also spiked 200% last week (12 vs. 4.0 avg), suggesting complaints cluster around construction-related code issues
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints with DOB permit filings and violations to identify whether spike correlates with specific projects or a pattern of unpermitted work
Interview DOB and local contractors about whether there is a shortage of qualified crews leading to rushed or improper work

themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints spiked dramatically 3 weeks ago to 3 complaints (up 1100% from a 0.2-complaint weekly average), the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, indicating neglected or abandoned properties becoming visible eyesores.
evidence: 3 lot condition complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35, highest z-score in dataset)
Spike is slightly older than this week but remains the single most dramatic statistical outlier
469 abandoned vehicle complaints over 90 days suggest ongoing property neglect across district
reporting_angles: Identify the specific properties flagged in the lot condition complaints and investigate ownership, tax status, and code violation history
Report on whether the city has enforcement capacity to address abandoned or neglected lots, or whether problem properties remain unaddressed for years

themes_detail.label: Root, Sewer, and Sidewalk Damage
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints reached 8 two weeks ago, up 121% from a 3.6-complaint weekly average, reflecting infrastructure wear that may affect pedestrian safety and building integrity across the district.
evidence: 8 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (121% spike, z-score: 5.11)
Street condition complaints remain elevated at 596 total over 90 days, indicating chronic infrastructure issues
1999 blocked driveway complaints suggest roots and debris are impeding access
reporting_angles: Partner with Department of Environmental Protection to obtain sewer backup data and tree-trimming schedules for the district
Document specific locations where sidewalk damage poses pedestrian safety risk and report on city's repair backlog
